title: Spatial models map malignant territories and immune exclusion in salivary gland cancer
summary: A preprint used scVI and cell2location models to integrate single-cell references with Visium HD measurements from four salivary-gland adenoid cystic carcinoma sections from three patients. The spatial analysis inferred ordered malignant-cell states, millimeter-scale tumor territories, enrichment of immune signatures in stroma, and B7-H4 transcript enrichment in tumor nests. Cell-type abundances and lineage ordering are model-based inferences; the small descriptive cohort requires larger-cohort, protein-level and clinical validation, and does not establish a treatment effect.
ai_technology: scVI variational-inference model; cell2location hierarchical Bayesian spatial deconvolution
organization: University of New Mexico; Centrillion Biosciences

evidence.tested: scVI/cell2location-derived spatial mapping was checked against histologic annotations and marker patterns; permutation-based territory analysis tested spatial organization against random mixing.
evidence.unknown: Only four sections from three patients were studied, and spatial bins are not independent patient replications. Model-inferred cell abundances/trajectories do not establish causal lineage transitions; larger-cohort, protein-level and clinical confirmation remain needed under the source conclusions.
evidence.ai_role: Learned scVI batch correction and cell2location probabilistic deconvolution mapped cell types to 10-µm spatial bins, enabling spatially resolved lineage and immune analyses.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 PDF: abstract; scVI latent-model training and cell2location reference/spatial-abundance Methods; selected territory, histologic/marker and immune-signature Results; limitations and affiliations. Supplementary analyses not independently reproduced.
